fact: The consolidated National Registration Act (Chapter 01:02, Act 26 of 1986) is an Act of Parliament that commenced on 31 December 1986 and was amended up to Act 11 of 2017 and S.I. 124 of 2017; it provides for the Registrar of National Registration to keep a national register of citizens aged 16 or over and for identity cards to be issued.

The National Registration Act, 1986 (No. 26), an Act of the Parliament of Botswana assented on 24 December 1986, commenced on 31 December 1986 and sets up a national register of citizens and lawfully resident non-citizens aged 16 or over, kept by the Registrar of National Registration, with an identity card issued to each registered person.

The Minister of Labour and Home Affairs told Parliament that the National Registration (Amendment) Act, 2025, an Act of Parliament amending the law governing the national identity card (Omang), provides that a passport or driving licence is used as identification while a defaced, lost or expired identity card awaits replacement.

The Minister of Labour and Home Affairs said the National Registration (Amendment) Act of 2025 now allows passports and driving licences as valid identification while identity cards (Omang) are being replaced; it is an Act of Parliament amending the national registration law.
